svg.title: True airspeed against altitude at a constant calibrated airspeed of 200 knots

desc.style: color: rgb(34, 48, 63); fill: rgb(0, 0, 0); fill-opacity: 1; fill-rule: nonzero; stroke: none; stroke-width: 1px; stroke-opacity: 1; stroke-dasharray: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; opacity: 1; font-size: 17px; font-family: Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-style: normal; text-anchor: start; dominant-baseline: auto; letter-spacing: normal; visibility: visible; paint-order: normal; marker: none;

svg.desc: At sea level TAS equals CAS at 200 knots. TAS then climbs steadily with altitude: 232 knots at 10,000 feet, 271 at 20,000, 319 at 30,000 and 386 at 40,000 feet — roughly two per cent more true airspeed for every thousand feet climbed. The curve is the compressible relation, not CAS divided by the square root of the density ratio.
